subject: Renewal: 16→32 GPU commitment and phased throughput guarantee
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@atlas-sys.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@atlas-sys.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity increase: interest in moving to 32 GPUs

Hi Dylan,

We're preparing our annual renewal and Atlas is planning to double our reserved capacity from 16 → 32 GPUs to support a Q4 product push. Before the renewal call next week we wanted to get an initial sense of:

- Reserved per-hour pricing for 32 GPUs (and how that compares to the 16-GPU rate).
- Whether Redwood can offer a phased ramp (keep 16 reserved at T0, then add 16 more within 60–90 days) while guaranteeing throughput targets as we ramp.
- Any SLA / throughput credit language you recommend for this scenario.

Attached is our high-level expected QPS/KPS profile (atlas_prod_qps_requirements.pdf). We expect sustained traffic growth; the ability to add capacity quickly is a priority. Looking for a 12-month renewal with the upgrade included.

Can you confirm ballpark pricing and whether a staged commitment is supported? Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Platform, Atlas Systems
phone: +1 415 555 0721

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@atlas-sys.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase: interest in moving to 32 GPUs

Elena —

Really appreciate the heads up and the attachment. Short answers first: yes, we can support a phased ramp and we can provide throughput SLOs tied to the reserved pool.

Ballpark commercial options (subject to final negotiation):
- Immediate swap: Commit to 32 GPUs at once, 12-month reserved term: $8.25/hr per GPU (monthly invoice).
- Phased ramp (recommended if you want a conservative rollout): Start with current 16 reserved at your existing rate, add the additional 16 as a scheduled augmentation over 60–90 days. The incremental 16 GPUs during ramp would bill at $8.75/hr per GPU until the ramp completes, then the blended 32-GPU rate of $8.25/hr would apply going forward.

Operational safeguards we propose for the staged approach:
- Throughput guarantee: We will guarantee a 99.5% token-generation success rate and a 99th percentile latency bound consistent with the attached SLA table.
- Ramp window: We’ll commit to provisioning the additional GPUs within the agreed 60–90 day window, with interim scaling (burst pool) available if traffic spikes.
- One-time ramp credit: If provisioning slips past the 90-day mark, Redwood will issue service credits equal to 5% of the monthly reserved fees for each 7-day period of delay (capped at one month).

I’m attaching a draft amendment for the capacity add (redwood_draft_amendment_32gpu_v1.pdf) and a simple SLA table (throughput-sla-table.xlsx) so you and procurement have language to review. Can Laura and I coordinate with your procurement next week?

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive — Dedicated & Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase: interest in moving to 32 GPUs

Elena — quick note on pricing structure and an alternative term that might help Atlas manage spend while getting the capacity you need.

Proposal A (Immediate 32):
- 32 GPUs reserved, 12-month term, $8.25/hr/GPU ⇒ estimated monthly committed cost: $191k (see attached spreadsheet).

Proposal B (Phased ramp w/ staged billing):
- Month 0–2: keep 16 reserved at your current committed rate, bill additional 16 as surge-reserved at $8.75/hr (discounted compared to on-demand).
- Month 3 onward: convert to full 32 reserved at $8.25/hr.
- If Atlas signs a 24-month term we can offer a 6% additional commitment discount on the 32-GPU rate.

We can also include a 30-day performance verification window after the ramp completes; if Atlas doesn't see the throughput improvements we committed to, we'll provide a one-time fee credit (amount negotiable).

Attached: throughput-sla-table.xlsx (detailed SLOs) and a sample cost workbook. Happy to walk through numbers on a call.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: dev.patel@redwood.ai

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 10:16:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal + capacity increase: interest in moving to 32 GPUs — draft amendment / SLA notes

Team —

I reviewed redwood_draft_amendment_32gpu_v1.pdf and the SLA table. A few legal/contractual items to flag before we send to Atlas procurement:

1) Service credits: the proposed 5% monthly credit per 7-day delay is fine, but we should cap total credits at 25% of the relevant monthly invoice to protect Redwood exposure.
2) Termination for convenience: Atlas wants staging flexibility; we should include a minimum 3‑month notice period before downgrades to protect capacity planning.
3) Liability and indemnity: add explicit language that performance guarantees exclude incidents attributable to Atlas (misconfiguration, third-party latency, network outages outside Redwood control).
4) SLA verification: require use of agreed monitoring endpoints and token-count methodology in the verification clause to avoid disputes.

I'm attaching a redline (internal) with these edits — will send a clean copy to procurement once we align on the cap and notice terms.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@atlas-sys.com>

Date: Fri, 06 Aug 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: 16→32 GPU commitment and phased throughput guarantee

Dylan/Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. Procurement reviewed Dev's notes and a couple of follow-ups from our side:

- Atlas can accept the proposed ramp credit structure but asks that the cap be lowered to 15% of the monthly invoice (we're trying to limit cost exposure if a ramp slips).
- For termination/downgrade notice, a 90-day notice is reasonable, but we need an option to reduce non-critical GPUs sooner in case of an emergency (we can include an emergency scale-down clause with a small fee).
- On exclusions: we'll accept the Atlas-attributable exclusion language but would like an explicit troubleshooting playbook and a named escalation contact for production incidents during the ramp.

If you can send a final redline with the adjusted credit cap (15%), emergency scale-down language, and the named escalation contact details, we can route to signature. We prefer DocuSign for execution.

Elena

Elena —

Thanks — we've aligned internally. Final items we agreed to put in the amendment:

- Credit cap adjusted to 15% of the monthly reserved invoice (per Atlas request).
- Emergency scale-down clause: Atlas may request an emergency reduction of up to 8 GPUs once per 12-month period; a nominal one-time processing fee equal to 0.5% of the monthly reserved bill will apply.
- Named escalation contact: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.ai) — 24/7 on-call for ramp incidents; runbook and monitoring endpoints will be shared in Confluence.
- Pricing and term: Phased ramp as discussed — incremental GPUs billed at $8.75/hr during ramp, convert to $8.25/hr/GPU once ramp completes; 12-month term. 24-month commit available with a 6% reduction on the 32-GPU baseline rate.

I uploaded a final redline and DocuSign package here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/7632190 (DocuSign link included). Please confirm and we'll schedule signature and a kickoff to schedule the ramp.

Next steps:
1) Atlas procurement confirms redline and routes DocuSign.
2) Once signed, Redwood schedules the initial provisioning and assigns Ben as primary on-call.

Looking forward — happy to jump on a call if helpful.

Best regards,
